title: Quick check: Data Quality for Model Training

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes data filtering and deduplication in the context of data quality for model training?
options: A fluent result is enough to establish correctness, so the input and assumptions do not need checking.
The concept can be implemented entirely in a prompt; application validation and testing are unnecessary.
Use the largest available model for every task and skip a baseline or documented acceptance criteria.

Data filtering and deduplication addresses how information is prepared, described, versioned, or governed. Validate the input, keep source and access metadata, handle duplicates and missing values deliberately, and test the downstream effect of a data change rather than treating the data pipeline as invisible plumbing.
questions.answer_key: Data filtering and deduplication addresses how information is prepared, described, versioned, or governed. Validate the input, keep source and access metadata, handle duplicates and missing values deliberately, and test the downstream effect of a data change rather than treating the data pipeline as invisible plumbing.
questions.explanation: Data filtering and deduplication addresses how information is prepared, described, versioned, or governed. Validate the input, keep source and access metadata, handle duplicates and missing values deliberately, and test the downstream effect of a data change rather than treating the data pipeline as invisible plumbing. This is why the lesson treats the concept as something to apply and verify, not as a guarantee of quality.

questions.prompt: Which practice gives the clearest evidence that data mixture design is working in data quality for model training?
options: Skip validation because a well-formatted answer implies the model followed the intended process.
Change the prompt, model, data, and settings at the same time, then attribute any difference to one cause.
Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
Test only one easy input, then assume the behavior generalizes to every language, user, and data source.
questions.answer_key: Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
questions.explanation: Data mixture design should be evaluated with evidence appropriate to its use. Representative tests and a baseline help reveal failures and avoid overstating what the example proves.

questions.prompt: A team applies data filtering and deduplication from data quality for model training and gets a plausible result, but it has not checked an edge case. What should it do next?
options: Increase model size and deploy immediately, without retaining a baseline or regression tests.
Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
Accept the result because confidence and fluency are reliable substitutes for measurement.
Remove guardrails or access checks to make the next run more likely to succeed.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
questions.explanation: A plausible answer is not proof. Controlled tests, evidence checks, and explicit uncertainty help identify incorrect assumptions and unsafe failure modes.
